Privacy Policy:

By providing my phone number to Vineyard City I agree and acknowledge that Vineyard City may send text messages to my wireless phone number for any purpose. Message and data rates may apply. We will only send one SMS as a reply to you, and you will be able to Opt-out by replying "STOP". 

No mobile information will be shared with third parties/affiliates for marketing/promotional purposes. All the above categories exclude text messaging originator opt-in data and consent; this information will not be shared with any third parties.

item.title: Mayor's Office
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Mayor’s Office supports City leadership and community programs. Its work includes Code Enforcement, Communications and Media, and City events.



Mayor Zack Stratton

ADDRESS:
125 S Main St.
Vineyard, UT 84059

EMAIL:
mayor@vineyardutah.gov
___________

TO SCHEDULE A MEETING OR SEND COMMENT:

Email: davidk@vineyardutah.gov
Phone: (385) 480-7807

___________

CODE ENFORCEMENT:

Ed Kennedy
Email: edk@vineyardutah.gov
Phone: (385) 307-3828

___________


MEDIA SPECIALIST:
For Press Inquiries call: (385) 480-7807

Brailee Tyler
Email: braileet@vineyardutah.gov
Phone: (801) 361-2361

___________

 

ABOUT THE MAYOR:
Zack Stratton is a sixth generation Utah County native who understands the importance of community, faith, and family. Raised in Orem, Zack grew up learning the value of hard work from generations before him. His great-great-grandfather helped settle the Provo Bench as a fruit farmer, and his grandfather, Herb Stratton, continued that legacy while serving as a teacher. Zack’s father, Keven J. Stratton, has carried the torch of public service as a longtime member of the Utah Legislature and now as a Utah State Senator. That heritage of service and stewardship is something Zack proudly carries forward.

Zack is the co-founder and CEO of Stratton Landscape Group, one of the region’s most successful landscape and construction firms. What began as a student-run startup at BYU has grown into a company with more than 250 employees and award-winning projects across Utah and the West. Zack also holds a master’s degree in business management from UVU and has overseen major public works—including city parks, commercial developments, and landscaping for temples of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. His leadership style is practical, hands-on, and focused on building things that last.

In every aspect of his life—from running a business to raising a family—Zack believes in fiscal responsibility, honest communication, and public transparency. Recently, he led a successful citizen referendum to stop the $35 million City Hall project in Vineyard. In just one week, over 500 residents signed the petition, resulting in the City Council canceling the plan. That experience reaffirmed Zack’s belief that government should always listen first and remain accountable to the people it serves.

Zack and his wife, Rachael, have lived in Vineyard for the past four years and are raising four children who are active in local events, sports, and church life. As Mayor, Zack is committed to ensuring Vineyard grows with purpose while protecting taxpayers, promoting transparent and accountable government, and making sure every resident's voice is heard and respected.

item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Council Vacancy Application

Applications must be completed and submitted in person at the Vineyard City Offices by 12:00 PM on September 11. A $50 filing fee is required at the time of submission.

Vineyard City Hall:

125 South Main Street, Vineyard, UT 84059

Monday - Thursday: 8am – 5pm
Friday: 8am – 12pm
_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

The City Recorder’s office consists of the City Recorder and Deputy Recorder.

The City Recorder's office is the custodian of all official city records including agendas, minutes, ordinances, resolutions, proclamations, agreements, contracts, and business licensing. The office updates and maintains the municipal code for public access. Records management is a key function of the office.

The City Recorder’s office also receives and processes GRAMA requests. The State of Utah established the Government Records Access Management Act (GRAMA) to allow the public to make a request for a record from the appropriate Utah government official or agency.

For police reports please contact the Utah County Sheriff's Office. Their form can be accessed here. 

The City Recorder’s office also administers all municipal elections, which are held on odd-numbered years.

Notary Services - appointment recommended.

item.title: Records Request
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
GRAMA (RECORDS REQUESTS)
The Government Records Access and Management Act, commonly known as GRAMA, was established by the state of Utah to allow the public to make a request for a record from the appropriate Utah governmental entity. This act can be found in 63G-2 of the Utah State Code. 

Almost all government records are subject to request. Upon receipt of a request the governmental entity will determine the classification and provide the records and/or a response. 

How to Fill Out a Request
A person making a request must submit a written request to the City Recorder who will send it to the department that maintains the desired record. 
The request must be in writing and must include your name, address, telephone number, email address, and a specific description of the records requested.  The request can be submitted by email, U. S. mail or in person. Links to our forms can be found below.

  • Submit a Records Request Form
  • Record Request Form (pdf)
  • Visit the State of Utah's Open Records Portal
  • Police Reports:
    • Utah County Sheriff's Office
    • Orem Police Department

Helpful Tips
GRAMA requests are designed to provide records, not answers to questions. Make sure they are specific and concise in order for us to quickly locate and identify the records requested. In accordance with state law you should receive a response from us as soon as reasonably possible but no more than 10 business days unless an extension is requested.

Requests may have fees associated with them depending on how the record is retrieved.

If you are denied a request there is an appeal process you can go through. Please visit Municipal Code sections 2.28.070 and 2.28.080. It is recommended that you keep a record of your request for the appeals process.

item.title: Basement Finish
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
A BUILDING PERMIT IS REQUIRED FOR FINISHING A BASEMENT

Thank you for your interest in pulling a permit from the Vineyard Building Department. Provided below is information to get you started on your project, but please don’t hesitate to contact us at 801-226-1929 or building@vineyardutah.org if you have additional concerns or questions.

WHY WOULD YOU WANT TO PULL A BUILDING PERMIT FOR YOUR BASEMENT FINISH?

A permit will ensure that your basement is built to code compliance and it will protect your family’s health and welfare. 

Having a code compliant basement finish may help you with any insurance claims should any mishaps take place in the future of your home. You also can’t sell your house for the full appraisal value unless your basement was finished with a permit.

Don’t want to do the work twice? Be aware that inspecting a basement finished without a permit requires that the drywall and insulation be removed in order for our inspectors to see the original work done. So it is more cost effective in the long run to pull your permit before you start your basement finish.

HOW TO SUBMIT FOR A BASEMENT FINISH PERMIT IN VINEYARD.

Submittals
The Vineyard Building Department accepts submittals both online and over the counter. You may submit online through the Building Portal or print a Building Permit Application and submit it in person. 

Parcel Information
If you are having difficulty locating your parcel information, you can find your lot #, subdivision, and phase on the Utah County Parcel Map. Just enter your address and city on the left-hand side and then click the little blue “land info” link.

Valuation
A valuation is required for federal and state agency reporting requirements. This valuation is the estimate of the cost of your labor + materials to finish your basement. 

Basement Walkout
If you are planning an exterior exit from your basement you will need to provide an engineering letter. You can contact any engineering company for this. Anytime you impact the foundation of your home, the City needs to ensure the structure will be engineered to support the load of the house above. 

Your permit submittal will also require a detailed plan of your stairs leading to the basement walkout, as well as a site plan indicating the location of your walkout in regard to your property lines. For questions about property lines and setbacks, please contact the Vineyard Planning Department.

Owner/Builder Certifications
An Owner/Builder Certification form is necessary if the work is being performed by the sole owner of the property. 

Plan Requirements
In order to expedite your plan review, please check your plans, supporting documents (such as engineering calculations), and application to be sure you have all the required information. 

Plans and supporting documents submitted online must be in a pdf file format. Plans submitted in person should be on pages no greater in size than 11" x 17."

Any plans reviewed or drawn by an Engineer must be sealed and signed by the Engineer.

Your plans do not need to be drawn by an architect. However, below is a good list of what needs to be shown on those plans.

PLAN REQUIREMENTS FOR BASEMENTS: (*Note: Any plans requiring Engineering must be sealed and signed by the Engineer.)

  • Dimensioned floor plans showing all wall openings, stairs, doors, closets, and other spaces.
  • Label the use of each room and space.
  • Include all spaces in the area you wish to finish with this permit
  • Identify load bearing walls. Typically, these are walls already constructed in the unfinished basement.
  • Identify any bearing walls being replaced by beams and provide the engineering for each.
  • Show all windows and give window size.
  • Identify all bedroom window well dimensions (i.e. 4 1/4’ wide by 3’ deep by 4’ tall) measured to the top of the well from the window sill. All bedrooms with window wells taller than 44” will need an attached escape ladder.
  • Show furnace, water heater, and other utility equipment.
  • Show smoke alarms in each bedroom and one in the area adjacent to the bedrooms.
  • Show a carbon monoxide (CO) alarm outside bedrooms. All smoke alarms and CO alarms must be wired in series to all alarms on all levels.
  • Show layout of electrical outlets in the rooms.
  • Show location of electrical panel serving the finished basement areas.
  • Show all plumbing fixtures, fireplaces, and other added equipment.

Plan Review Process

  • Plans are reviewed on a first come first serve basis regardless of complexity.
  • The review for a basement permit submittal is typically completed within one week from the time it was submitted, but is subject to workload.
  • At any time you may check on the status of your plan review by going to the building web portal.
  • For any questions on how to navigate the web portal please see the portal handout.         
  • Plan review communications (such as comments, corrections, or approvals) will be sent to the email provided on the building permit application. 
  • Once the review is complete and the plans have been approved the building fees can be paid and permit can be issued.
  • For questions on permit fees please contact the Building Department.

Additional Information to Consider

  • If you currently have or are planning to have a second kitchen in your basement, a Second Kitchen Acknowledgement form will be required to be recorded. This will be covered in more detail by the Plans Examiner during the plan review process. 
  • If you are finishing your basement for the purposes of using it as a rental unit please contact the Vineyard Planning Department for instructions on how to apply for Accessory Dwelling Unit Accessory Dwelling Unit license.
  • At this time, we can accept cash, check or card as forms of payment. Please be aware that all card transactions will have an additional 3% charge.  

Please contact the Vineyard Building Department with any questions throughout the process.

item.title: Streets and Stormwater
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded: Vineyard City Public Works Department provides top-notch service to our residents, with a focus on improving their quality of life by maintaining clean, safe, and hazard-free roadways. The Streets and Stormwater Division is responsible for overseeing all of the city's public roads. The division provides snow removal, street sweeping, asphalt maintenance, signage, striping, shoulder maintenance, and storm drain maintenance. To ensure efficient and cost-effective snow and ice removal, Vineyard City follows a comprehensive Snow Removal Policy that takes into account the unique variables presented by each weather event. Our staff is dedicated to delivering the highest level of service and responsiveness to citizen requests and concerns, contributing to the overall well-being of Vineyard City residents.

Vineyard City dedicates substantial financial resources annually to a diverse range of construction projects aimed at enhancing our community. These capital improvement initiatives encompass the enhancement of our streets to optimize mobility and the upgrading of our stormwater system. Additionally, funds are allocated for the construction or rehabilitation of vital structures like fire and police stations, as well as recreational facilities. These strategic and enduring investments play a pivotal role in bolstering our economic vitality and cultivating livable neighborhoods.

Spanning various stages—ranging from planning and design to procurement, construction, and closeout—these projects exhibit a dynamic timeline, spanning from several months to several years. Despite their diverse sizes and scopes, these endeavors serve as tangible manifestations of Vineyard City's commitment to shaping a prosperous and sustainable future. They embody the ongoing transformation of Vineyard City, symbolizing our dedication to building a better tomorrow for our community.

item.title: Grounds Maintenance
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
As Vineyard City offers a robust and top-quality Open Space and Trails to its residents. And, in an effort to enhance the aesthetic appeal and usability of public spaces and facilities Vineyard City's initiative focuses on regular maintenance, beautification services, partnerships, and active volunteer involvement to elevate the quality of life for residents. Beyond promoting health through well-maintained parks and trails, the plan aims to establish Vineyard City as a unique and appealing place, fostering community connections in clean and inviting spaces. By instilling pride among residents, the city anticipates increased support for local government initiatives. The implementation involves a collaborative approach between the Public Works and Parks & Recreation departments, deploying trained staff to ensure cleanliness and health in public areas. Actively engaging the public in the preservation of open spaces and conducting regular surveys to gather feedback are integral components of the plan. As Vineyard City continues to grow, this initiative seeks to adapt open spaces in alignment with evolving community needs, ensuring a vibrant and sustainable environment for all residents.

Vineyard City established the Tree Manual to regulate urban forest health, aligning with the city's plan and codes. The objectives include maximizing canopy coverage, preventing conflicts with infrastructure, and promoting environmental benefits. The manual emphasizes proper tree placement, maintenance, and encourages similar practices on private property. It aims to create attractive landscaped spaces for public use while providing a standardized list of acceptable tree species for Vineyard's public areas.

Fleet Maintenance
Vineyard City's Fleet and Facility Maintenance division manages the upkeep of city vehicles, equipment, and infrastructure. This includes regular maintenance, repairs, and inspections to ensure operational efficiency and safety. They oversee vehicle maintenance schedules for various departments and maintain city facilities to uphold safety standards. Through efficient management, the division supports Vineyard City's operations and infrastructure needs.

item.title: Splash Pad
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
350 N 100 E, Vineyard, UT 84059
The Splash Pad closed for the season September 12, 2026.
It will reopen for the season around Memorial Day 2027.

HOURS

Monday-Saturday

10:00 AM - 8:00 PM

*Weather permitting

 

SPLASH PAD RULES

  • This facility is unsupervised – play at your own risk
  • Adult supervision is recommended
  • Do not drink the water
  • Running, boisterous, or rough play is prohibited
  • No climbing or hanging on equipment
  • No animals allowed in the splash pad at any time
  • No glass containers, skateboarding, bicycles or scooters allowed
  • Children not toilet trained must wear swimming diapers and tightly fitting plastic pants
  • Splash pad may close at any time due to weather or maintenance concerns
  • In an emergency, dial 911
  • For problems with the splash pad, dial 385.215.4060
  • Be courteous. Take turns.
  • Only one child allowed on the slide at a time.

item.title: Skatepark Fundraiser
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vineyard City has been putting forth efforts towards getting an All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park near the existing City Hall Building (located at 125 S. Main St., Vineyard)! If you would like to support the cause, please click on the “Donate Here” link above. All donations are allocated to a restricted and reserved Vineyard City Skate Park fund.

All credit card payments are subject to an approximate 3% fee (this amount may be taken out of your donation to cover the charge). Otherwise, you can submit a donation via check or cash to Vineyard’s Finance Department at the Vineyard City Hall (125 S. Main St, Vineyard) during our normal business hours of Monday-Thursday 8am-5pm and Fridays 8am-Noon. If you write a check, please write it out to Vineyard City and write “Skate Park Donation” on the Memo line.

All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park: Following the request for proposal process, Vineyard City chose to partner with Hunger Skateparks to create an All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park design. We would like to thank the Vineyard Community for the feedback you provided regarding the features you would like to see in the park. Public engagement efforts included an in-person Open House, two surveys (with a total of 249 submitted responses), and various social media posts (with a total of approximately 75 comments).

In February of 2026, the Vineyard City All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park final design was completed. The 16,000 square foot facility is to be located on City-owned property just southeast of the Vineyard City Hall Building (125 S. Main St, Vineyard, UT 84059). Durable cast-in-place concrete construction, which is considered the industry standard for municipal skate parks, will help ensure long-term performance, reduce maintenance needs, and improve safety in various ways for users.

The overall scope of this project shall consist of two phases. Phase one includes an All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park, 24 added parking stalls (one of which being ADA-compliant), an ADA-compliant ramp park entrance, approximately 375’ of added Asphalt Trail to connect two existing trail networks, landscaping, a restroom facility, utility line extension for potential outdoor lighting, two benches, two signage posts, and three single-inverted-U bike racks. Phase two may include an asphalt pump track, pavilion shade structure adjacent to the All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park, and outdoor lighting surrounding the pump track and skate park.

Due to the Vineyard City All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park being designed to have terrain suitable for both beginner and advanced users, this recreational amenity is intended to serve users of varying ages and skill levels. The park will be welcoming of skateboarders, scooter-riders, roller bladers, BMX bikers, and adaptive riders.

The total estimated project cost for completion of Phase 1 is $1,420,000. In March of 2026, Vineyard City submitted a Utah Outdoor Recreation Grant application to request for a 50/50 match amount of $694,500. Pending the receipt of this grant award in May of 2026, Vineyard City plans to begin construction in the Summer of 2026, with the Phase 1 grand opening to occur in June of 2027!

To fund Vineyard City’s required portion of the 50/50 grant match, the Vineyard Mayor and City Council approved via resolution on March 10th, 2026 to allocate current and future Vineyard RAP Tax funds to build the facility.

Not only will this facility expand outdoor recreation within Vineyard City for teenagers and young adults, but it will also provide an individual-based recreation opportunity to the public and drive economic impact for the Community. The location of the facility will allow for convenient oversight with public safety offices nearby to help promote responsible use and stewardship of the facility.

Please forward any questions to Vineyard’s Parks & Recreation Director (Brian Vawdrey) at: brianv@vineyardutah.gov


Green Area = Potential Vineyard City All-Wheels Concrete Skate Park
Red Area = Potential Vineyard City Asphalt Pump Track
Yellow Area = Potential 8’ Asphalt Trail connecting two existing trail networks
Black Area = Additional 24 Asphalt Parking Stalls (one of which being ADA)
Pink Area = Outdoor Restroom Facility

*All professional concept designs shown above were provided by American Ramp Company for Phase 1 & 2 full-buildout*

item.title: Community Development
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Community Development vision is to promote a high quality of life to the community. It is responsible for overseeing the growth and development of Vineyard City, while enhancing the quality of life for citizens. It is composed of the following divisions:

Accessory Dwelling Units – ADU
Are ADU's allowed in Vineyard?
Yes, they are allowed in Vineyard if they meet the requirements listed in VZC 15.34.060. https://vineyard.municipalcodeonline.com/book?type=zoning#name=15.34.060_Accessory_Dwelling_Units.   
What is Vineyard City looking for during an ADU Inspection?
An ADU inspection will look for some of the following areas:

  • Lot size 6000' ft minimum
  • Dedicated exterior entrance
  • Dedicated ADU parking stall
  • Fire alarm
  • Bathroom with exhaust fan
  • Full kitchen
  • Window egress for each bedroom
Where are they allowed?
  • As a detached structure with at least 12,000 square foot lot 
  • Within a home provided the lot is at least 5,200 square feet and meets all applicable building and fire codes.  
  • Mobile homes, travel trailers, boats, or similar RVs are not permitted as an ADU.  
What about parking?
A  single-family dwelling with an accessory dwelling unit shall provide a minimum of four (4) onsite parking spaces located on a paved surface or approved driveway. Only driveways or parking pads containing a minimum length of eighteen feet (18’) may be counted toward required onsite parking. The minimum length of a driveway counting toward onsite parking shall not include any land associated with street rights-of-way, sidewalks or public property/access. All onsite parking spaces shall contain a minimum width of eight feet (8’). Property owner parking shall not be parked tandem with tenant parking and tenant parking shall not be parked tandem with owner parking. The area dedicated to onsite parking and driveway surfaces shall be limited in compliance with VZC Section 15.38.030(2)(b). 
How many people can live in an ADU?
One family or up to four unrelated individuals may reside in an ADU.  
How to apply?

Apply for an ADU here.

How do I set up an ADU inspection?
Once you apply here our team will reach out to schedule an inspection.
How often will I need to renew my ADU license?
Every two years you will need to renew this license, at which time a $50 renewal fee will be due and you will need to schedule an inspection with the Code Enforcement Officer. After you pass the inspection, your application will be approved?
Can I appeal a code enforcement finding or any related penalty fees?
Yes. If you would like to appeal a code enforcement finding or related penalty fees, please fill out the Code Enforcement Appeal Form. Our team will review your appeal and follow up with you regarding the next steps.
Fencing
What are the height requirements for fencing?
No fence, wall, or similar structure can be erected on any required rear or side yard to a height in excess of six (6) feet. Additionally, fences located on the front property line or on the side property line within the front yard cannot be higher than forty-two (42) inches (Section 1623)
How should my fencing be designed?
All walls and fences are to be compatible with the surrounding landscape and the architecture and building materials of buildings on and adjacent to the property (Section 1623)
What fencing restrictions apply to corner lots?
In all Zoning Districts, no view obstruction, including a sight-obscuring fence, wall, sign, other similar structures, and landscaping which exceeds two (2) feet in height can be placed on any corner lot within a triangular area formed by a diagonal line connecting lines located at the curb line thirty (30) feet from the projected intersection of such curb lines (Section 1628)
What fencing restriction apply to driveways?
In all Zoning Districts, no view obstruction, including a sight-obscuring fence, wall, sign, other similar structures, and landscaping which exceeds two (2) feet in height can be placed within a triangular area formed by a diagonal line connecting lines located at the curb line and driveway line twelve (12) feet from the projected intersection of such lines (Section 1629)
What are the fencing requirements for a pool?
If your swimming pool is more than eighteen (18) inches deep, then you must have a protective fence that is no less than four (4) feet six (6) inches tall surrounding it (Section 1716).
• Additionally, All outdoor jacuzzi tubs, or other similar small pools, may be protected by a solid locking cover in place of a protective fence,However, if you do not have a solid locking cover, a protective fence must be used instead (Section 1716).
Pet and Animal Requirements
What is considered a household pet
A household pet includes domesticated animals and birds ordinarily allowed in a dwelling unit and kept for company or pleasure of the owner, including, but not limited to dogs, cats, and caged birds. Household pets do not include domestic livestock or fowl, as defined herein or inherently or potentially dangerous animals, fowl, reptiles or exotic animals 
How many pets may I own
For any given household, there may be up to four (4) dogs or cats, or combination thereof (Section 5-2-22)
What should I know if I want to raise livestock or fowl?
No domestic livestock or domestic fowl shall be kept on any lot that is less than one (1) acre, and may be allowed as a permitted use in the A-1 and R&A-5 zoning districts (Section 1712).
The number of livestock or domestic fowl that may be kept where the area is used exclusively for the keeping of domestic livestock or fowl is one (1) acre, shall be as follows:
  • Limited to a maximum of one (1) domestic animal per acre (Section 1712). 
  • Fowl may be kept on lots equal to, or larger than one (1) acre, provided the number of fowl maintained does not exceed twenty-five (25) fowl for each acre (Section 1712).
  • Domestic livestock, fowl, and other animals, but excluding all prohibited animals, may be kept on lots of five (5) acres or larger without restriction on the number of domestic livestock or animals kept (Section 1712)
What are the requirements for maintaining livestock and fowl?
No barn, stable, shelter, corral, coop, pen, or run in which domestic livestock or fowl are maintained shall be closer than one hundred (100) feet to any residential structure located on adjacent lots (Section 1712).
  • All yards, barns, shelters, cages, areas, places, and premises where domestic livestock, animals, or fowl are kept shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition so that flies, dust, or odors do not disturb the health of any person or animal or create a nuisance to any adjoining property (Section 1712).
  • Additionally, all household pets shall be kept in such a manner that they do not disturb the peace, comfort, or health of any person or animal (Section 1711). 
Building Height & Setbacks
How is building height measured?
Building height is measured from the top of the back of curb to the highest point of the building or structure.
How high can I build my house?
No primary building within any district can be built to a height less than one (1) story entirely above grade. Additionally, no primary building within a residential district can be built above thirty-five (35) feet (Section 606)
How are setbacks determined?
A setback is the required distance by which a building or part of a building is set back from the property line, and is measured from the property line to where the building begins. Often, there are required setbacks from the sides, front, and rear of the property line. Setbacks vary based on zoning district, and can be found in the table in Section 606 of the Zoning Ordinance.
Are there any exceptions that are made for objects obstructing setback areas?
All required setback areas shall be open to the sky and unobstructed except for permitted and approved accessory buildings and structures, and for projections of sills, unenclosed steps, unwalled stoops, bay-windows, unenclosed porches and similar building features, provided that such features do not encroach more than three (3) feet into the required setback area (Section 1622).

• Additionally, walls and fences are permitted, so long as they comply with the requirements of Section 1622 and required approval by a Land Use Authority
Cul-de-sacs Frontage
What is the required lot frontage for a lot fronting a cul-de-sac?
For lots which front upon a curve or cul-de-sac, the lot frontage may be reduced to not less 
than fifty (50) feet (Section 1618). Lot frontage is all the property fronting on one (1) side of the 
street between intersecting or intercepting streets, measured along the street line 
How does lot frontage differ from lot width?
Lot width is the shorter of horizontal distance between side lot lines, measured at the required front yard setback line or rear setback line (Definitions - Lot Width). Additionally, lot width conforms to the setback of the lot frontage (Refer to graphic below)
Accessory Buildings
What is an accessory building?
An accessory building is a building customarily incidental and clearly subordinate to the primary building and located on the same lot as the primary 
building 
• Accessory building and accessory uses can only be authorized concurrently with, or following, the establishment of the primary building or primary use (Section 1703).
Where can I build an accessory building?
Accessory buildings are only permitted within the rear yard of an established lot (Section 1703). 
  • The required setbacks for accessory buildings are three (3) feet from the sides and rear of the property line, and six (6) feet minimum distance from the primary building. Accessory buildings are limited to a maximum of twenty five (25) feet in height, but the side and rear setbacks must increase one (1) foot for every foot above fifteen (15) feet in height (Section 606)
Am I allowed to live in an accessory building?
No accessory building can be used as a permanent dwelling unit, except as allowed for accessory dwelling units (Section 1703)
Is there anything else I need to know about  accessory buildings?
No mobile home, travel trailer, boat, or similar recreational vehicle is permitted to be used as an accessory building (Section 1703).
  • Additionally, no shipping container, cargo container, shipping crate, box, trailer, or similar moveable piece of equipment or object is permitted to be used as an accessory building (Section 1703).
  • No accessory buildings can be rented, leased, or sold separately from the rental, lease, or sale of the primary building, except as allowed for accessory dwelling units (Section 1703)

item.title: Planning & Zoning
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Planning and Zoning Division is where the vision of the City’s future is crafted and carried forward. It is where big ideas start to become a reality through development. It provides direction and leadership of the implementation of goals, objectives, and policies of Vineyard City. Planning and Zoning is also responsible for the orderly development of the City and the administration of various land use regulations, development applications, and design standards.  

Zoning Administration: Grand construction projects and ideas start to become a reality here. Staff spend a considerable amount of time and effort in assisting in all aspects of development including large commercial projects, residential additions or accessory building and uses, and land uses. They also serve as a professional support staff for the Planning Commission and in helping to develop and interpret the Vineyard Zoning Code. Much of the built environment by these ordinances and codes and how they are applied.  

Long Range Planning: The City puts a lot of effort into working with residents and stakeholders creating a long-lasting vision for the future. This includes maintaining a General Plan for the City that includes goals and policies, as well as several Master Plans that work in supporting these goals and policies in greater detail.

item.title: Code Enforcement
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
THE CODE ENFORCEMENT PROGRAM WORKS WITH RESIDENTS, PROPERTY OWNERS, AND BUSINESS OWNERS TO MITIGATE AND RESOLVE NEGATIVE IMPACTS IN THE CITY OF VINEYARD. THROUGH VOLUNTARY COMPLIANCE AND COOPERATION, OUR CODE ENFORCEMENT TEAM WORKS TOWARDS RESOLVING NEGATIVE CONDITIONS TO ULTIMATELY MAKE THE CITY OF VINEYARD AN EVEN BETTER PLACE TO LIVE. BUILDING BETTER NEIGHBORHOODS THROUGH DEDICATED SERVICE

Code Enforcement promotes and maintains a safe and desirable community consistent with health and safety regulations, and provides residents with sustainable property values and a lower crime rate. This is done by assisting residents and property owners to be in compliance with the City codes in a friendly, fair, and impartial manner.

MISSION STATEMENT:
The mission of the City of Vineyard Code Enforcement is to provide a safe, healthy, and quality life for its citizens while at the same time promoting a high degree of professionalism and respect for human dignity.

VISION STATEMENT:
To be a strong and effective organization through open communication, teamwork, mutual respect, and a partnership with the community, willing to pioneer innovative approaches through community enforcement.

item.title: Parking
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Use the above links to apply for a city parking permit. Currently, the city has a parking permit program for the following areas:
  • Providence Neighborhood
  • 100 West and 470 North in the Springs Neighborhood
Permit Rules and Regulations
  • Permits are only valid for parking on designated public streets
  • Street parking is prohibited during snowfall
  • Vehicles parked illegally may be towed or booted at the owner's expense
  • Permits may be revoked as a penalty for violations
  • Parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis. Once all designated parking spaces are occupied, no additional vehicles can be accommodated


Parking Permit FAQ
  • How many permits am I able to purchase? 
    • Providence and Springs neighborhoods are able to purchase up to 3 permits per household. 
  • If I am a landlord, should I register and account or should my tenants?
    • We encourage whoever is living at the property to sign up for the permit. As part of the sign-up process, the account holder must personally review and agree to the rules and regulations set by Vineyard City. Additionally, they may need to update vehicle information or renew their permit in the future, and creating an account for them could lead to complications if they are unfamiliar with how to manage these actions.
  • How many vehicles can be listed on 1 permit?
    • You can list all of your vehicles on 1 permit, however, only 1 vehicle per permit is able to be activated for street parking. Be sure that the vehicle that is parked is the vehicle and license plate that you have selected on your account.
  • How long is my permit valid for?
    • Permits are valid for 1 year from date of activation. When your permit is about to expire, you will receive email notifications from our vendor letting you know to renew.
  • Do I have to purchase an entire year pass?
    • Yes, all permits are sold on a 1-year basis. If you are moving and no longer need the pass, you can let the city know and we can void the pass going forward.


Edit Form

Parking Permit Program Petition

The Parking Permit Program Petition requires at least 75% of your neighborhood to agree to implement. You can find out more information about the program here: https://cms3.revize.com/revize/vineyard/OVERNIGHT%20PARKING%20PROGRAM%20(2).pdf If you are wanting to implement or remove the parking permit program in your neighborhood, please use the form below.

Document Center

The Document Center provides easy access to public documents. Click on one of the categories below to see related documents or use the search function.

item.title: Short Term Rental
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Short-Term Rentals Are Not Permitted in Vineyard

Vineyard City does not permit short-term rentals (such as Airbnb, VRBO, or similar vacation rental platforms) in residential zoning districts.

Properties advertised or operated as short-term rentals are considered to be in violation of the Vineyard Zoning Code and may be subject to enforcement actions and civil penalties.

Applicable City Code

VZC 15.12.050 – District Use Table
VZC 15.12.040 – Vineyard Zoning Map

Enforcement

If Vineyard City determines that a property is being used as an illegal short-term rental, the property owner may receive:

- A notice of violation
- Civil penalties
- Additional daily penalties

Listings advertised on platforms such as VRBO, Airbnb, or similar websites may be used as evidence during the enforcement process.

Questions?

If you have questions regarding short-term rental regulations or zoning requirements, please contact:

Ed Kennedy
Code Enforcement Officer
Monday–Thursday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM
Phone/Text: 385-307-3828
Email: edk@vineyardutah.gov
Office: 707 E Mill Road, Suite #202, Vineyard, UT

item.title: Business Licensing
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your interest in locating your business in Vineyard, Utah! The rapidly-growing community of Vineyard is an excellent place to locate your business.

WHO MUST OBTAIN A BUSINESS LICENSE
If you engage in any business out of a physical location within the boundaries of Vineyard, you are required to maintain a valid, unexpired business license.  This includes home-based businesses.  Please note that registering a business name with the State of Utah Department of Commerce does NOT license a business with Vineyard.

HOW TO APPLY
Please click on the appropriate link for your business license type to access the online application, and reach out to Business License Specialist Kelly Kloepfer with any questions.

item.title: Utah County Sheriff's Office
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Utah County Sheriff’s Office currently provides all law enforcement services for Vineyard City. Vineyard City and The Utah County Sheriff’s Office have enjoyed a wonderful working relationship for many years and look forward to continuing this partnership.

There are currently 17 Sworn Personnel/Deputies, who provide 24/7 law enforcement services to the community. The staffing plan includes a Chief, four Sergeants, two Detectives, ten Patrol Deputies, and one School Resource Officer. Along with the sworn personnel, the Vineyard Division is also staffed with a three-quarter-time Office Specialist. Our depth is even greater with the support of the Utah County Sheriff’s Office team of specialized units. These units include Utah County Metro SWAT, K-9 Teams, Investigations Division, Accident Investigation Team, Search and Rescue, Emergency Services, and Recreation Teams.

Vineyard City has seen exponential growth over recent years, which has made it one of the fastest growing communities in Utah. With its approximately 22,000 residents, Vineyard is a relatively young city with many families and children. With this unique demographic and rapid growth, The Sheriff’s Office is taking a proactive approach to providing the best public safety and service by implementing programs such as Neighborhood Watch, NOVA, Public Safety Fairs, etc.

The Sheriff’s Office and Vineyard City are partnering to provide the best, most efficient and cost-effective law enforcement services available to the great residents of the community. The Utah County Sheriff’s Office is honored to serve the residents of Vineyard.

item.title: R.A.D. Women Self-Defense Classes
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
R.A.D. Women classes are coming to Vineyard! These free courses are offered in affiliation and partnership with R.A.D. Systems of Self-Defense and the Utah County Sheriff’s Office.

About the Course

The Rape Aggression Defense (R.A.D.) System is a comprehensive, women-only course that teaches realistic self-defense tactics and techniques. The course begins with awareness, prevention, risk reduction, and risk avoidance before progressing to hands-on defense training.

Participants will learn how to visually identify vulnerable areas, physically respond to an attack, and create opportunities to escape a violent encounter.

Course Details

  • Who: Females ages 12 and older

  • Dates: March 1, 8, 15, and 22, 2027

  • Time: 6:00–9:00 p.m. each Monday

  • Length: Four classes totaling 12 hours

  • Location: Vineyard, Utah

  • Cost: Free for Utah County residents

The exact class address will be provided to registered participants by email before the course begins.

Important Registration Information

Please read the following information before registering:

  • Registration requires a commitment to attend all four classes and complete the entire 12-hour course.

  • A separate registration form must be completed for each participant.

  • Participants ages 12–14 must have a parent or guardian attend every class with them.

  • Registration confirmation will be sent by email within one week of registering.

Register for the Course

Space may be limited. Complete the online registration form to reserve your place.

REGISTER FOR THE R.A.D. WOMEN COURSE

Physical or Medical Accommodations

Participants with medical or physical conditions requiring an accommodation should contact the Utah County Sheriff’s Office before the course. Staff will discuss available support and work to provide a safe, empowering educational experience whenever possible.

Women at any stage of pregnancy may attend and observe the course but may not participate in its physical portions.

Questions?

For questions before, during, or after registration:

  • Email: vineyarducso@gmail.com

  • Phone: (385) 200-1501 during regular business hours

item.title: UCSO Vineyard Citizens Academy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
UCSO Vineyard Citizens Academy registration is NOT YET OPEN. Watch the UCSO - Vineyard social media for announcements and registration opening.

For questions or concerns, please reach out to the UCSO Vineyard Community Coordinator: beccak@utahcounty.gov

USCO Vineyard Citizens Academy will be held Wednesdays starting February 24, March 3, 10, 17, 24 & 31 2027

The UCSO Vineyard Citizens Academy is an opportunity for community members to learn more about the Utah County Sheriff’s Office, meet the people behind the badge, and better understand the services provided to our community.

Participants will get an inside look at law enforcement operations, including patrol procedures, investigations, communications, emergency response, crime prevention, and other areas of public safety. The academy encourages open communication, builds positive relationships, and provides insight into the challenges and responsibilities of law enforcement.

Participants must be 18 or older. By registering, participants commit to attending the academy in its entirety.

Join us for an engaging, hands-on experience and discover what it takes to serve and protect our community! Space may be limited, so please complete the registration form to reserve your spot.

Not to be confused with the one time event, Nov. 4th Vineyard Mini Academy: The citywide Vineyard Mini Academy is a separate event where you can learn about City departments and services. No registration is required for the Vineyard Mini Academy.

item.title: Utility Billing
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Rate Changes Effective January 1, 2026 

Dear Vineyard Residents, 

We want to inform you about an upcoming adjustment to utility rates, which will take effect on January 1, 2026. This change is essential to support the long-term sustainability and efficiency of water and wastewater services. 

Water and Sewer Use Fees 

Vineyard has financial agreements in place to fund critical upgrades to the water and sewer infrastructure. These agreements include modest annual adjustments – 2% for water services and 5% for sewer services – to ensure the city meets inflationary demands while also maintaining reliable operations for our growing community. 

Additionally, the city’s wastewater treatment provider, Timpanogos Special Service District (TSSD), recently increased its treatment rates by 15%. As Vineyard is one of 10 municipalities served by TSSD, this increase is a direct pass-through cost beyond local control. It reflects the rising cost of delivering these essential services. 

Transportation Utility Fee 

Vineyard City is reinstating the Transportation Utility Fee to ensure the continued funding and sustainability of the City’s Transportation Utility Fund. As part of our review process, a rate study was conducted to identify fair, data-driven rates that ensure the Transportation Utility Fund can operate sustainably. As an enterprise fund, this account is required to support itself, meaning the services it provides must be funded directly by the fee. 

The Transportation Utility Fee functions as a utility charge for our road system. Revenue from the Transportation Utility Fee is dedicated to the maintenance, operation, repair, and improvement of local streets and transportation infrastructure. This includes essential services such as asphalt maintenance, sidewalk repairs, traffic signal operations, snow removal, and projects that support pedestrian and bicycle safety. 

Reinstating this fee provides a reliable, long-term funding source to keep Vineyard’s transportation network safe, functional, and well-maintained. 

We understand that rate adjustments can be challenging, and we remain committed to transparency and ensuring that every dollar supports the safe and efficient delivery of vital utilities to Vineyard residents. Thank you for your understanding and support.

item.title: Redevelopment Agency
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
The Vineyard Redevelopment Agency (RDA) is a Community Reinvestment Agency for Vineyard City. Authorized by the State of Utah, reinvestment agencies are formed to oversee redevelopment and revitalization in communities for targeted “project areas.” Utah has over 90 such agencies in cities across the state. These agencies are used to help cities grow their economy, build public projects, fix up old or damaged areas, and improve homes, businesses, and shopping areas. To do this, cities must have an agency like the RDA to manage these resources.

FORMATION
The Vineyard RDA was formed in 2009 to oversee redevelopment of the former Geneva Steel Mill–a former industrial site that shut down and went bankrupt. This left behind a blighted “brownfield” site with significant demolition and environmental clean-up needs. It has taken many years of work to prepare the area for different future land development uses. The Geneva Urban Renewal Project Area is 2,055 acres, or nearly 70% of the entire city. It stretches from the northernmost boundary of the city south to Center St. and from the lake on the west to Geneva Road on the east.

OVERSIGHT
The RDA is overseen by a board made up of the Vineyard City Council who makes decisions related to the designated “project area.” The RDA follows state laws that govern Community Reinvestment Agencies and govern the process for various tax revenue rules related to redevelopment.

PURPOSE
The purpose of the reinvestment agency is to eliminate industrial blight by rehabilitating the area into a vibrant and economically beneficial part of the community. This is done by encouraging and facilitating redevelopment of the site including:

  • Remediating the land through environmental cleanup and demolition work
  • Investing in new public infrastructure including transportation, public utilities, and community open space
  • Facilitating commercial and housing construction
  • Attracting economic development and jobs to the area

The Vineyard RDA follows the “project plan” first adopted in 2011 to guide the selection of projects to fund or incentivize the construction of housing, mixed use developments, commercial development, local infrastructure, and other economic development opportunities. Under state tax laws, the RDA is able to direct a portion of property tax revenues called “tax increment financing” to pay for some redevelopment costs for a period of time. Each phase of the project area can use tax increment revenues for 25 years.

DEVELOPMENT
Development in the RDA area is centrally located in Utah Valley, with easy freeway access. If you are interested in bringing your business to this prime location please contact our Community Development Team.

The RDA Board meets as needed, usually following a City Council meeting.

item.title: Vineyard 101: Mini Academy
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vineyard 101 Mini Academy

Meet the people. Ask questions. Get to know your City.

Discover how Vineyard works and connect with the people who help keep our community running! Join us for an evening of conversation with City staff, where you can visit department tables, ask questions, and learn about the services and projects shaping Vineyard.

Wednesday, November 4, 2026
5:30–7:30 PM

707 E Mill Road, Suite #201
Vineyard, UT 84059

A New Format for a Familiar Program

Vineyard 101 Mini Academy replaces the City’s previous Vineyard Citizens Academy with a condensed, one-day experience. This new roundtable and open-house format brings City departments together in one place, making it easier for residents to meet staff and learn how each department serves the community.

What to Expect

  • Meet City staff: Get to know the people behind Vineyard’s services.

  • Visit department tables: Chat directly with representatives from each department about their work.

  • Ask questions: Bring your questions about City services, processes, and projects.

  • Explore what’s happening: Learn about current efforts and opportunities to get involved.

No registration is required. Stop by anytime between 5:30 and 7:30 PM!

Vineyard 101 Mini Academy is a Citywide event and is separate from the UCSO Vineyard Citizens Academy, which focuses on Sheriff’s Office operations and requires registration.

item.dc:creator: admin

The Youth City Council (VYC) is in session; 12–18 year old residents are invited to join. This is a great opportunity to make new friends, plan and participate in city events and service projects, and gain experience in leadership and civic duties. You can submit your intent to join through the link above. You will need to download the application and waivers below and turn them into the City Recorder's office before you can participate in any Youth Council activities. 

The purpose of the Vineyard Youth City Council is to provide training and opportunity to local youth to interact with the City Council and other important organizations, to allow for an opportunity for input from local youth to local government, and to deal with local issues impacting Vineyard's youth. The program is a volunteer program with two appointed Youth Council Advisors and under the direction of the delegated city staff. The Vineyard Youth City Council shall communicate information on current City issues, hold meetings, and report back to the City Council. VYC is a great opportunity to serve the community and meet new friends. For more information or to get the meeting dates and times, call 801-226-1929.

item.title: Vineyard Cares Board
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Vineyard Cares is a community coalition run by a community board and city staff member. Our mission is to prevent and reduce substance misuse as well as spread awareness regarding mental health issues among youth and families living in Vineyard, UT. Vineyard Cares is working to create an inclusive and thriving community where mental, social, emotional, and physical wellness are prioritized, empowering residents to lead fulfilling and healthy lives

BOARD VS. COALITION
The Vineyard Cares Board is responsible for making decisions and maintaining the coalition as a whole. They act as a voice for the coalition, determining where the coalition focuses attention and funds. The board reports to key leaders such as the Mayor and funders and oversee the bylaws of the coalition.

The Vineyard Cares Coalition is made up of local residents and businesses who want to participate in planning events and programs related to substance abuse awareness. They meet monthly to coordinate responsibilities and plan activities or classes for the community.

item.title: Development Review Commission
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
PURPOSE
The purpose of the DRC is to assure that any proposed use, activity, building or structure is consistent with the General Plan and complies with all requirements of the City’s Land Use Ordinances, including this Ordinance, and all other applicable Ordinances and requirements.

MEMBERSHIP
The DRC shall consist of seven (7) members, the Chair of the Planning Commission, the City Manager, the Fire Marshall or designee, and the heads of the departments of Building, Community Development, Engineering, and Parks and Recreation or their designee. The Fire Marshall and Vineyard Public Safety department shall advise the DRC on all land use decisions

item.title: Pedestrian Safety Commission
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Pedestrian Safety Commission

Help make Vineyard safer for everyone! Applications are now open for five regular members and two alternates to serve on Vineyard’s Pedestrian Safety Commission.

Formerly the Active Transportation Commission, the commission has been renamed and reorganized with a renewed focus on the safety of people walking, biking, using mobility devices, and traveling through Vineyard’s streets, crossings, sidewalks, and trails. All seats are open, and former members are welcome to apply.

What the Commission Does

The commission advises the Mayor and City Council on pedestrian safety by:

  • Identifying safety concerns at crossings, intersections, school routes, and other public spaces.

  • Reviewing traffic and safety information.

  • Recommending safety improvements and traffic calming measures.

  • Supporting public education and coordination with City staff, schools, and public safety partners.

Time Commitment

The commission will hold one regular meeting each month and may meet more frequently as needed. Members should also be prepared to review meeting materials and participate in commission responsibilities.

Appointments are anticipated to be completed by the end of November 2027, with the first meeting planned for early December.

Apply to Serve

Interested in making a difference? Complete the short application to share your contact information, why you would like to serve, and whether you can make the time commitment.

Apply for the Pedestrian Safety Commission

City staff will review applications and reach out regarding next steps. Thank you for your interest in helping make Vineyard a safer community!

item.title: City Dump Passes
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
In lieu of a bi-annual cleanup, Vineyard will provide dump passes on a yearly basis for residents to use at North Pointe Solid Waste Special Service District. In January, residents will receive a Vineyard dump pass in the mail with two punches available. Residents will be able to use the two punches at any time throughout the year.

How to Get Your Pass
Vineyard dump passes will be sent to residents (renters and owners) who pay sanitation fees through their utility bill. (HOAs that provide their own trash services do not qualify.) To know if you qualify, look for "Sanitation" on your utility bill.
*If you pay sanitation fees for recycling only, you aren't eligible for a pass.

If you don't receive your dump pass in the mail and you qualify for one, come into the city offices to pick up a pass (bring photo ID and proof of address). 

How to Use Your Pass
To use your dump pass, present the pass and photo ID at North Pointe. They'll verify your identity and punch your pass to signify it's been used.

The dump is open:
Monday–Friday: 7:00am–5:30pm
Saturday: 7:30am–3:30pm

North Pointe has limitations on what you can dump. Please review their FAQ page to see what they do and don't accept.

How to Correct Your Pass
If you received a Vineyard dump pass in the mail, but it has outdated information (i.e., the wrong name), bring it into the city offices with photo ID and proof of address, and we can correct our database and provide you with an updated pass.


We're excited to switch to this new system and hope it will provide greater flexibility for discarding waste. If you have any questions or concerns, please reach out to us at 801-226-1929.

Vineyard City is a proud partner to One Kind Act a Day and a Certified City of Kindness as of January 2024. Vineyard was the first city to take this pledge, demonstrating a commitment to community and unity. Residents, staff, and businesses have made a commitment to make kindness a cornerstone of daily life in Vineyard.

One Kind Act a Day, a nonprofit dedicated to promoting kindness and community unity, has inspired individual acts of kindness across Utah. Vineyard’s unique approach aims to integrate kindness into every aspect of city life, creating an environment where compassion and empathy thrive.

item.title: Vineyard City Fireworks
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Pioneer Day Fireworks Statement from Vineyard City 2026

Personal fireworks are permitted only on July 24 and July 25, between 11:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m., and only within the designated fireworks discharge areas shown on the MAP BELOW.
View the interactive map here.

Note: Fireworks may only be discharged on private property with the permission of the property owner.
Please note that The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints does not permit fireworks on its properties, including church buildings and parking lots.

As we celebrate Pioneer Day, Vineyard City reminds residents that personal fireworks are permitted only within the designated fireworks discharge areas approved by the City and Fire Department.

If you're planning to use personal fireworks, please help keep our community safe:

  • Use fireworks only within the designated discharge areas.

  • Keep a bucket of water, hose, or fire extinguisher nearby.

  • Light fireworks on a flat, nonflammable surface and away from dry vegetation.

  • Never aim or throw fireworks at people, buildings, vehicles, or animals.

  • Fully extinguish and properly dispose of used fireworks once they have cooled.

  • If a fire starts or an emergency occurs, call 911 immediately.

These restrictions were established in coordination with the Fire Department under the Governor's Executive Order and are intended to balance holiday celebrations with the safety of our residents, firefighters, and natural areas.

Thank you for doing your part to keep Vineyard safe this Pioneer Day. We wish everyone a fun, safe, and happy holiday!

item.content:encoded:
How do I get a pass?
Visit Vineyard City Hall with proof of residency (such as a utility bill, lease agreement, or ID) to receive your physical Eco-Pass today!

How much does it cost?
The Eco-Pass costs $59 per month. Payments can be made at Vineyard City Hall or online via Podium (a 3% fee applies to credit/debit card payments). If payment is not received by the 3rd business day of the month, the pass will be deactivated until payment is made.

What does the Eco-Pass include?
The Eco-Pass provides unlimited travel for one calendar month on local buses, express buses, TRAX light rail, Streetcar light rail, bus rapid transit, and FrontRunner commuter rail.

item.title: Neighborhood Watch
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
What is a Neighborhood Watch Program?

A Neighborhood Watch program is implemented by a group of people living in the same area who are working to make their neighborhood safer. Each neighborhood’s program is managed by an Area Leader who is appointed by their neighbors. The area leader and residents work together with local law enforcement representatives from the Vineyard Division of the Utah County Sheriff’s Office to reduce crime and improve residents’ quality of life. Citizens are trained to recognize and report suspicious activities in their neighborhoods and can implement crime prevention techniques such as home security, operation identification, and other methods. Neighborhood groups can also work to provide emergency and disaster preparedness, neighborhood clean-ups, and coordinate with faith-based organizations to address the neighborhood’s needs

Why start a Neighborhood Watch Program?
Law enforcement officers have responsibility for the whole city and cannot be present on every street corner. Citizen involvement is an essential component of combating crime. Residents of your neighborhood know what is happening in your community. By partnering with Vineyard’s UCSO deputies, neighborhoods can prevent and fight crime in the most effective ways.

What's the time commitment? 
Neighborhood Watch groups have regular meetings to plan how they can accomplish their goals and responsibilities, Groups are required to have a minimum of one meeting per year and can meet more often, as needed. These meetings will include discussing, planning, or reporting projects and goals selected by the neighborhood.

How to start a Neighborhood Watch Group

First, determine if there’s a need and/or interest in having a Neighborhood Watch program by talking with your neighbors.
Then, contact the Utah County Sheriff’s Office (UCSO) and inform them of your neighborhood’s desire to start a program.
Other initial steps include:
  1. Reading the Neighborhood Watch Starter & Leadership Handbooks (available online or at the City Office).
  2. Designating an Area Leader.
  3. Completing area leader information and a map.

item.title: 2025 Election Information
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
FINAL ELECTION RESULTS!

On November 18, 2025, the City Council held a special session to certify the results of the November 4, 2025, General Election.
Those elected to office are:
Mayor – Zack Stratton
Councilmembers – David Lauret, Parker McCumber, and Jacob Wood.
In accordance with state code 10-3-201(2), they will take office on January 5, 2026, at 12 o’clock noon.

CASTING OF LOTS
On June 26, 2024, the Vineyard City Council voted to put a change in government to a vote of the people. At an election held on November 5, 2024, Vineyard Residents approved a change in government from a five-member council to a six-member council. As a result of the change in government and in accordance with Utah State Code 10-3b-606, those three (3) Council members were to be elected to office. Also, in accordance with Utah State Code 10-3b-6-606(4) of those three (3) Council members, one is to serve a two-year term, which is to be chosen by lot. This was done at the November 18, 2025, City Council Special Session. Parker McCumber drew the 2-year seat. David Lauret and Jacob Wood will retain the 4-year seat.

Certification of the 2025 General Election

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

ELECTION RESULTS

https://electionresults.utah.gov/results/public/utah-county-ut/elections/general11042025

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

We have two candidates who have withdrawn from the 2025 General Election, Hayden Morris (Council) and Hector Hernandez (Mayor). Their withdrawal forms can be found under their candidate information. 
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

General Election Results:
Utah County will be posting preliminary election results at 8:00pm and 10:00 PM on election day Tuesday, November 4, 2025.
Friday November 7, 2025 at 5:00 PM
Wednesday November 5, 2025 at 8:00 PM
Wednesday, November 12 at 5:00 PM
Friday November 14, 2025, at 5:00 PM
Tuesday November 18, 2025 at 12:00 PM
Official Canvass will be held on Tuesday November 18 at 6:00 PM
_______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

With the official ballot drop box at City Hall (125 South Main Street, Vineyard, Utah) now open, we want to remind everyone that City Hall is now considered a voting location under Utah election law. As such, no electioneering is permitted within 150 feet of the drop box. This restriction helps ensure a neutral environment for voters and maintains the integrity of the election process.

For reference, Utah Code §20A-3a-501(1)(a) defines electioneering as:

“Any oral, printed, or written attempt to persuade persons to refrain from voting or to vote for or vote against any candidate or issue.”

This includes, but is not limited to, displaying campaign signs (Including cars, bikes, etc.), distributing literature, wearing campaign apparel (Shirts, hats, buttons, etc.), or engaging in conversations intended to influence a voter’s choice within the restricted area. We appreciate your cooperation in helping us maintain a fair and accessible voting environment for all residents. To help clarify where the restriction applies, below is a photo showing the approximate 150-foot boundary around City Hall. The marked area represents where no campaign activity or materials may be displayed while the ballot drop box is in operation.

Additionally, on November 4, 2025, the City Hall building will be an active polling location, and the 150 feet restriction will apply to the City Hall building as well as the County drop box. Please see the map for the full restricted area.



If you have any questions about the restricted area or how it is measured, please don’t hesitate to contact the Recorder’s Office at 385.338.5183.

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Drop Box Locations

______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Logic and Accuracy Testing
______________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

General Election Notice

The Utah County Elections Division gives notice of the General Election that will be held on Tuesday, November 4, 2025.

Voters must be citizens of the United States, residents of the voting precinct in which they are voting, and 18 years old or older by the date of the election to participate. All eligible voters will receive their ballot by mail approximately three weeks before Election Day.

A sample ballot and other information relating to the election, including polling places, polling place hours, instructions regarding how an individual with a disability may obtain information on voting in an accessible manner, and qualifications of voters may be obtained from the following sources:
1.    Visiting the Utah County Elections Division’s website: https://vote.utahcounty.gov
2.    Visiting the Statewide Electronic Voter Information Website: https://vote.utah.gov
3.    Visiting the Utah County Elections Division Office
4.    Calling the Utah County Elections Division: (801) 851-VOTE (8683)
5.    Emailing the Utah County Elections Division: elections@utahcounty.gov
6.    Contacting your City Recorder

A public demonstration will be held to test the voting devices and tabulation equipment being used for the noticed election. Anyone who would like to witness the testing is invited to attend, beginning at 10:00 a.m. on October 9, 2025 at the Utah County Ballot Center - 100 E Center Street ROOM LL700 Provo Utah.

All eligible voters will receive their ballot by mail approximately three weeks prior to Election Day.
We strongly encourage voters to return their ballots via the conveniently located drop boxes listed on our website at: vote.utahcounty.gov/voting-locations

The Polling Locations (listed below) will be open from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. on Election Day for any voter in Utah County to return their ballot or vote in person. Accessible voting machines are available.

Here are your candidates in ballot order:

Vineyard will be holding a Primary Election on August 12, 2025, to nominate six (6) City Council candidates to move on to the General Election. You will be voting for up to three (3) people. 

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________


Important Dates to Remember

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

DECLARATION OF CANDIDACY

The Declaration of Candidacy Period begins Monday June 2 and runs through June 6, in the Vineyard Elections Office, 125 South Main Street. The hours will be Monday through Friday 8:00 am to 5:00 PM on a first-come, first-served basis (no appointment necessary). See filing qualification below.

ALL CANDIDATES MUST FILE IN PERSON!
If you will out of the state for the entire week of the declaration period, please contact the City Recorder’s office at 385.338.5183 or 385.432.7214 for further details.

We ask that you bring the Conflict of Interest Form and if necessary, the Name Variation Form with you when you come in to  file your declaration of candidacy.

Sample Declaration Packet - this a sample only. The Election's Office will provide you with the forms you will need to fill out.

Conflict of Interest Disclosure Statement - Please fill this form out and bring it with you when you come in to file your declaration of candidacy.

Name Variation Guide and Form - this form is only need if you wish to use a nick name or derivative of your legal first name. Please fill it out and bring it with you when you come in to file you declaration of candidacy.

Nomination Petition Form- this form is only needed if you are nominating someone to run for an elected office. This form must be turned in during the declaration period, June 2-6, 2025, 8 AM to 5 PM.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

2025 VINEYARD CITY MUNICIPAL ELECTION NOTICE

Pursuant to Section 10-3-301(2)(a) of the Utah Code, notice is hereby given that the Municipal Offices in Vineyard, Utah to be voted on in the 2025 Municipal General Election are:

  • Mayor – to be elected at-large to serve a four-year term.
  • City Council Members – three (3) council members will be elected at-large to serve a four-year term with the exception that one member will serve a two-year term. The two-year term will be determined by lots immediately following the election canvass. (UCA 10-3b-606(4))

A Primary Election will be held, if necessary, on Tuesday, August 12, 2025. The General Election will be held on November 4, 2025.

A Vineyard City resident who is interested in becoming a candidate must file a Declaration of Candidacy between June 2 and June 6, 2025. Declarations of Candidacy must be filed, in person, with the Vineyard City Recorder's Office at Vineyard City Hall, 125 South Main Street, Vineyard, Utah, Monday through Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. A $50.00 filing fee is due at the time of filing.

Election information may be obtained at:

  • Vineyard City Recorder’s Office: Pamela Spencer 338.5183, pams@vineyardutah.gov or Tony Lara 385.432.7214, tonyl@vineyardutah.gov
  • Utah County website: https://vote.utahcounty.gov/home
  • Utah State website: https://vote.utah.gov

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
Filing Qualifications

A person filing a declaration of candidacy for a city office must be (per Utah Code Section 20A-9-201 and 203):

  • A United States citizen at the time of filing;
  • A resident of Vineyard City for the 12 consecutive months immediately preceding the date of the election (or a resident of an area recently annexed into Vineyard City);
  • A registered voter.

In accordance with Utah Constitution Article IV, Section 6, any mentally incompetent person, any person convicted of a felony, or any person convicted of treason or a crime against the elective franchise may not hold office in this state until the right to hold elective office is restored under Utah Code Section 20A-2-101.3 or Section 20A-2-101.5.

item.content:encoded:
Please note: This league is specifically designed for individuals 8–12 years old who have intellectual disabilities. Thank you for registering for Vineyard City's 2025 Street Hockey League! You can expect to hear from your child's coach/Vineyard Administration by Saturday, September 13th.

Age: 8-12
Season: Thursday, September 24th–Thursday October 30th
Registration ($65): July 1st–August 31st *Includes shirt & stick*
Non-Resident Fee: $10
Late Fee: $10

6 Games, Thursday 5:15–6:05
Games will take place at Vineyard's Gammon Park
1 game per week
Each gameday will consist of a 20-minute practice and one 17-minute scrimmage
5v5 with goalies - Participant dependent

50' x 90' Court
50" x 42" Goal
No official score will be kept

Game Schedule
Available on Tuesday, September 9th @ quickscores.com/vineyardutah.

Referees
Vineyard Recreation will provide referees and coaches. Any parent participation is greatly appreciated as you know your child's needs best.

Teams
Each team will have a maximum of 12 players. Teams will be decided each week.

Coaches
We are looking for help from volunteer coaches. If you are interested in being a volunteer coach, please select the option to do so during online registration. Volunteer head coaches may receive up to a 50% credit for future programming for their child's participation in the league (to be granted following the season). Volunteer assistant coaches may receive up to a 25% credit for future programming for their child's participation in the league (to be granted following the season). *Each team is to have 1 head coach and 1 assistant coach.*

In addition to our parent volunteers we will have paid staff to help with coaching and building these kids up.

Age Cutoff
All participants must be aged 8–12 on October 2, 2025.

Additional Questions Contact
Zach Baty
Recreation Manager
p: 385.455.7398
a: 125 South Main Street
